intervals.label: partial operation
intervals.note: Only 2 of 5 stations confirmed actively collecting data as of the cited 2024 paper. Currency pass 2 (2026-10-25), no status change. The 2024 paper's 'planned upgrade' happened at least in part: arXiv:2509.18368 (September 2025) says "In 2024, two of the five ARA stations received DAQ upgrades" and describes the "2024-2025 season upgrades" of the ATRI-based DAQ, with RFSoC-based DAQ "foreseen in the coming years". Newer ARA abstracts treat the array as five stations 'taking data for over a decade' (ARENA, June 2026) with analyses of the 2013-2023 dataset and 'nearly 30 station-years of livetime' (arXiv:2603.00341, Lepton Photon symposium proceedings submitted 27 February 2026); none reports which stations are live in 2026 or the outcome of the 2025-26 and 2026-27 Antarctic seasons, so the 'reduced-scale operation' wording (2 of 5 live in the 2024 paper) is kept and may now be conservative.
intervals.quote: Currently A3 and A5+PA are currently collecting data; other stations are awaiting a planned instrument upgrade

summary.plain: Five separate stations of radio antennas buried in the ice near the South Pole, each listening on its own for the radio flash of an ultra-high-energy neutrino.
summary.technical: 5 autonomous ARA in-ice radio stations, 100-200 m deep, deployed 2012-2018 near the South Pole; only A3 and A5+PA (with its low-threshold phased array) confirmed actively collecting data as of the 2024 collaboration overview paper.

technology.quote: ARA comprises five independent autonomous stations, with an additional low threshold phased array merged with station 5
technology.value: Autonomous in-ice radio (Askaryan-effect) detector stations, each an independent array of radio antennas buried 100-200 m deep in the ice
